description: A school principal must approve the operating and privacy plan for a student-run morning announcement broadcast, including its audience, archive period, student hosts, and oversight records, with input from the journalism teacher, instructional technology coordinator, and school counselor.

shared_context.S1: The school is preparing a pilot in which students will produce a live morning announcement broadcast each school day.
shared_context.S2: The draft plan would stream the broadcast publicly, keep recordings for 90 days, allow any journalism student to host, and use the library as the studio.
shared_context.S3: Ms. Patel has authority to approve the operating and privacy plan before the pilot begins.
shared_context.S4: As part of the school's routine activity-approval process, Ms. Patel asks the journalism teacher, instructional technology coordinator, and school counselor to review the draft before signing it.

PF1.text: Mr. Greene completed the broadcast practicum with six students, identified in the class roster as J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, and J6; only those six students have completed the school's camera, microphone, and live-broadcast training, so they are the students he can authorize as hosts.

PF2.text: Ms. Novak confirmed that the district's approved student-media platform supports an internal-school audience with a 30-day archive and requires moderator approval before each broadcast; the public-stream setting and 90-day archive in the draft are not approved district configurations.

PF3.text: Mr. Ellis reviewed a current court-related privacy order naming student K7 that prohibits the school from recording or broadcasting K7's image or voice; K7 is enrolled in journalism and must be excluded from both the host roster and any recorded broadcast, with the exclusion documented in the activity file.

acceptance_conditions: The broadcast must be restricted to the internal school audience.
Recordings must be retained for exactly 30 days.
The host roster must contain exactly J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, and J6.
K7 must be excluded from the host roster and recordings.
A trained-student authorization record must be created.
A platform moderation configuration record must be created.
A privacy-exclusion record must be created.

decisive_facts.why: The six completed practicum students change the host roster from any journalism student to exactly J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, and J6 and require a training authorization record.
The approved platform configuration changes the audience to internal_school, changes retention to exactly 30 days, and requires a platform moderation configuration record.
The privacy order changes the exclusion list to exactly K7, requires K7 to be kept out of recordings, and requires a documented privacy-exclusion record with the fact cited.
